meta.title: Why You'll Sometimes Find Two Starbucks Blocks Apart
meta.hook: A beautiful corner can still be a terrible Starbucks location if traffic, rent, and demand do not work together.
meta.description: Starbucks uses geospatial and demographic data — foot traffic, income levels, population density, competitor locations — to decide where to open stores, treating site selection more like an engineering problem than intuition. That data-driven approach is also why you'll sometimes see two Starbucks locations only blocks apart: a model determined both spots could independently support a store.

scenes.narration: A beautiful corner can still be a terrible Starbucks location if traffic, rent, and demand do not work together.

scenes.narration: Starbucks' annual disclosures treat site selection and lease economics as material risks because a weak location is expensive to unwind.

scenes.narration: That also explains why stores may cluster: nearby locations can serve different traffic patterns or reduce congestion at one busy shop.
